extension” which is located in the directory of AutoSched AP. It enables further functions, actions or 
action lists, and rules . There are additional entries in the options file (cf. Figure 1), e.g.

evidence.content:
7 
 
In addition, in the file “attach.txt” the distribution of the first TTF is defined. In the column FOADIST, 
the distribution type is stated (here exponentially distributed). The mean of the first TTF (FOA) and the 
time units are needed (FOAUNITS). 
 
Figure 7 - downcal.txt 
3.1.2. Scheduled Down Times: Preventive Maintenance (PM) 
Used files: pmcal.txt, attach.txt 
The representation of PMs works almost in the same way as for breakdowns (cf. Figure 8). Here, two 
types for the Mean Time Between PM (MTBPM) values are distinguished (PMCALTYPE). The PM is time-
based for diffusion, lithography, and metrology represented by mtbm_by_cal to consider the calendar 
time. For all other tool groups, the PM is counter-based by applying mtbpm_by_pieces, i.e., a PM must 
be executed after processing a prescribed numb er of wafers. Hence, the corresponding numbers and 
units are needed in the columns MTBPM and MTBPMUNITS. Note that no special probability 
distribution is defined for MTBPM (the default is constant). However, the time -based PMs are 
practically launched as Mean Time Before PM, so that the PM duration itself is included in the MTBPM 
value. 
A continuous uniform distribution is used to represent the TTR value that requires values for the two 
parameters MTTR and MTTR2 (mean and offset) and the time unit (MTTRUNITS). For instance, each 
30 days a monthly PM and each 91 days a quarterly PM is modeled for the station family 
DefMet_BE_33 in the lines 2 and 3. In attach.txt file, line 13, a monthly PM is allocated to the station 
family (RESTYPE = stnfam). Moreover, counter-based PMs are also applied for each station family, i.e., 
the used RESTYPE is stnfam and the RESNAME is the name of the tool group (see file “attach.txt” or 
Figure 6, line 92). The prescribed number of wafers is valid for each individual tool of the tool group. 
The distribution of the first PM for the tools of a tool group is defined in the column FOADIST (see file 
“attach.txt”). The constant distribution means that the first PM for the tools of a tool set is evenly 
distributed based on the value in the column FOA. For example, a FOA value of 80 days with four tools 
lead to PMs for to ol 1, 2, 3, and 4 at the following days: 20, 40, 60, and 80. For counter -based PMs it 
works in the same way, but FOAUNITS are not necessary.
